subtitle: The model has to earn every bit of complexity it uses.

steps.label: RIDGE (L2): sum of squared coefficients
steps.sub: Shrinks all of them toward zero

steps.label: LASSO (L1): sum of |coefficients|
steps.sub: Can push some to EXACTLY zero -- selects features

code:
X, y = make_regression(n_samples=120, n_features=40, n_informative=4, noise=40)
X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te = train_test_split(X, y, train_size=60)
# 40 coefficients, only 60 training rows, only 4 features really matter
caption: alpha=0 recovers plain OLS. Larger alpha = more shrinkage, simpler model.

code:
#         train R²   test R²   nonzero coefs
# ols       0.919    -0.645        40
# ridge     0.729     0.492        40
# lasso     0.681     0.636        10
caption: OLS is WORSE than predicting the average on test data. Lower train, higher test = the point.
OLS fits noise everywhere. Ridge squeezes toward zero. Lasso zeros most out entirely.

steps.label: THE PENALTY PUNISHES COEFFICIENT SIZE
steps.sub: Size depends on units -- unfair without scaling

code:
lcv = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LassoCV(cv=5)).fit(X_tr, y_tr)
print(lcv[-1].alpha_)            # 4.583 -- chosen automatically
print(lcv.score(X_te, y_te))    # 0.638, 11 features kept
caption: Never tune alpha by peeking at the test set -- RidgeCV / LassoCV do this honestly.

steps.label: RIDGE: many small, correlated effects
steps.sub: LASSO: a few features matter, need sparsity
